clinical_observations.content: sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. Upon initial observation, sabrina displayed a cheerful and cooperative demeanor but exhibited significant variability in her attention span, especially during repetitive tasks. Muscle tone was assessed as within normal limits, and she demonstrated a functional range of motion across all assessed joints. Nevertheless, sabrina's performance was notably impacted by frequent distractibility, necessitating continuous verbal and occasional visual cues for task redirection. She was more responsive to self-directed activities, showing increased engagement and initiative. Fine motor coordination and visual-motor skills were identified as areas of concern, with standardized tasks requiring hand-over-hand assistance for successful completion. Testing validity was affected by these factors, necessitating several modifications, including extended time and frequent breaks, to ensure optimal performance assessment.
